title: Derived pullback cohomology where a connective object is locally free in one degree
statement: Let g:T'→T be a morphism of schemes, E∈D(O_T) as in [def-pc-derived-category], and i a natural number. Suppose H^n(E)=0 for every integer n<0. Suppose every point t in the image of g has an open neighbourhood U and a natural r (allowed to depend on t) such that H^q(E)|U is zero for natural q≠i and H^i(E)|U is finite locally free of rank r, in the sense of [def-pc-invertible-in-degree-zero]. Then H^i(Lg^*E) is isomorphic to g^*H^i(E), for the ordinary pullback of [def-pc-module-pullback] and derived pullback of [def-pc-derived-pullback]. This is a statement about arbitrary connective derived objects and does not assume a proper morphism, a sheaf F, or a perfect-locus condition.

proof.text: Take W to be the union of the open neighbourhoods in the hypothesis. Exactness of open restriction preserves the negative vanishing; the given natural-degree vanishing covers the other degrees. Standard truncations identify E|U with H^i(E)|U placed in degree i. Truncation maps are canonical, so these descriptions agree on overlaps through the cohomology sheaf and identify E|W with H^i(E)|W placed in degree i. This is the cohomology-sheaf gluing step in the perfect-locus proof, and does not require E perfect once the local cohomology hypothesis is given.

Finite local freeness makes H^i(E)|W flat. The shifted single complex therefore computes its derived pullback by ordinary termwise pullback. Since range(g) lies in W, factor g through W, use derived pullback composition and the ordinary pullback composition isomorphism, and take degree-i cohomology. The result is the global isomorphism H^i(Lg^*E)≅g^*H^i(E). The empty open, rank zero, and varying local ranks need no exclusions.
